assessments.reasoning: The HTTPS original at data.norge.no/nlod/en/2.0 declares English HTML and credits the Norwegian Digitalisation Agency. Its capture SHA-256 8c9abba2b7498f057e3f78bcf4a41d9c7328b12e5bd08ff85b274d18cc0d0862 matches the claim. The title and §10 identify edition 2.0. Section 2 grants conditional permission to copy, modify and distribute information.

The Index's SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 includes terms for relevant data. Its License row requires identifiable text, an edition and a controlling source. The Agency's 2.0 text supplies all three. The Index document governs that mapping criterion and gives separate requirements for acceptance.

challenge.method: Compared the 2.0 document with the 1.0 original at the same host. Checked the title against §10, distinguished the ministry's future-version authority from the Agency's publication role, and tested the Index's License criterion against the operative grant.
challenge.results: The shared family name and similar §2 language could cause a mistaken merge. The distinct 2.0 digest, title and sole-version reservation reject that merge. Section 10 names the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation in its future-issuance provision. That role is consistent with the Agency publishing this representation.

limitations: The active lifecycle value describes the intended mapping. Current admission, application to a particular work, redistribution rights and installation eligibility require distinct evidence.
The identity is confined to the captured English HTML. Norwegian-language representation and compatibility fall outside the finding.
reasoning: The Agency's English HTML title identifies “Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) 2.0”. Under the heading “10. New versions of the licence”, the operative provision expressly allows a licensor to specify “solely version 2.0”. Section 2 supplies the grant for covered information. Applying SCES §§1–4, the digest identifies the representation, the publisher origin and credit establish attribution, and the operative text establishes the edition and licensing function required for the Index mapping.
